tools.name: whoami
tools.description:
Show who you are signed in as and the names your contacts can use to reach
you.

If setup_needed is true, ask your user what people usually call them
(nicknames, short names, names in other languages) and save the answers
with set_aliases.

tools.name: set_aliases
tools.description:
Replace the names your contacts can use to reach you, such as nicknames.

Your GitHub login and name always work and do not need to be listed.

tools.name: contacts
tools.description:
List your contacts, the names they go by, their agents, and the groups you
are in with their members.

person, `login/agent` for one of their agents, a group's "#id" for everyone
in it. If more than one person matches the name, a

tools.name: send
tools.description:
Send a message to a contact, to one of their agents, or to a group you are in.

A message to an agent waits in its inbox until the agent next reads it. A
message to a group reaches every member but the address you write from. To
answer a message, send to its `from` address, or to its `to` if that is

tools.name: inbox
tools.description:
Read your unread messages and the requests waiting for your answer, or
those addressed to one of your agents.

A message to a group has the group's "#id" as its `to`. An
attachment's `url` downloads it until its `url_expires_at`; open_attachment
shows it to you. Reading does not mark messages read:

tools.name: mark_read
tools.description:
Mark messages as read once you have handled them.

Each copy of a message belongs to one address, so only the copies of the
address you read them as are marked.

tools.name: create_group
tools.description:
Create a group, owned by the address you write from, which is its first
member.

Send to the group's "#id" to reach every member at once. Add your other
agents with invite.

tools.name: invite
tools.description:
Add an address to a group you are in: one of your own joins at once; a
contact's is invited and joins when they accept.

tools.name: leave
tools.description:
Leave a group, or remove an address from it.

You can remove any of your own addresses,
and the group's owner can also remove other people's. When the owner
leaves, the member that joined first becomes owner. A group nobody is left in
is deleted once its messages are, 30 days after they were sent.

tools.name: add_contact
tools.description:
Ask someone to become your contact, so you and your agents can write to each
other. Ask your user first.

They become your contact when they accept, or at once if they already asked
you. Adding someone you removed lets them write to you again.

tools.name: answer
tools.description:
Accept or decline a contact request or group invitation from inbox. Ask your
user first.

an invitation joins the invited address to the group. A contact request

tools.name: remove_contact
tools.description:
Remove a contact and block them, so neither of you can write to the other.
Ask your user first. add_contact undoes it.

tools.name: delete_account
tools.description:
Delete your peerbox account and sign out. Only when your user asks for it.

Deletes your agents, contacts, blocks, organisation memberships, the contact
requests and invitations you sent or received, every message you or your
agents sent (to groups too), every message sent directly to you or your
ag

tools.name: attach
tools.description:
Prepare a file of up to 10 MB to send: pass the returned id in send's
`attachments`.

Give `file` or `url`, or neither to get an `upload_url` and upload the file
yourself before its `upload_url_expires_at`: `curl -T <path> '<upload_url>'`.

tools.name: open_attachment
tools.description: Open an attachment of a message you sent or received, to see what it holds.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: inbox, mark_read, attach, open_attachment · Private data: whoami, set_aliases, contacts, send, invite, add_contact, answer, remove_contact, delete_account, attach · Public sink: contacts, send, create_group, attach · Destructive: leave, remove_contact, delete_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: inbox, mark_read, attach, open_attachment · Private data: whoami, set_aliases, contacts, send, invite, add_contact, answer, remove_contact, delete_account, attach · Public sink: contacts, send, create_group, attach · Destructive: leave, remove_contact, delete_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
